question: Who was the autobiographer of ‘Ace against Odds’?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sania Mirza**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Sania Mirza** is a professional Indian tennis player who has been a former world No. 1 in doubles.
 
• She has won six Grand Slam titles in her career.
 
• She is considered one of the most successful female Indian tennis players and one of the highest-paid and high-profile athletes in the country.
 
• The autobiography, **'Ace against Odds'**, was published in July 2016 and it chronicles her journey and achievements in the world of tennis.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mithali Raj**

 
 
• Mithali Raj is an Indian cricketer and the captain of the Indian women's national cricket team in Tests and ODIs.
 
• She is the highest run-scorer in women's international cricket.
 
• She is the only female cricketer to surpass the 6,000 run mark in Women's One Day Internationals.
 
• She is often regarded as one of the greatest cricketers in the history of women's cricket.
 
 
 
• **PV Sindhu**
 
 
• PV Sindhu is an Indian professional badminton player.
 
• She is the first Indian woman to win an Olympic silver medal in badminton.
 
• She has won medals at multiple tournaments including the Olympics and on the BWF circuit, including a gold at the 2019 World Championships.
 
• Sindhu is considered one of India's most successful sportspersons.
 
 
 
• **Saina Nehwal**
 
 
• Saina Nehwal is an Indian professional badminton singles player.
 
• A former world no. 1, she has won over 24 international titles, including eleven Superseries titles.
 
• She has represented India three times in the Olympics, winning a bronze medal in her second appearance at the London 2012 Olympics.
 
• She is credited for increasing the popularity of badminton in India.
